description.narrative: On 24 June 2026, two strong earthquakes, measured at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, with epicentres reported near Morón, Carabobo State. Preliminary information indicates damage to residential and commercial buildings, including reports of structural collapses in parts of Caracas and infrastructure damage in several affected areas. Critical damage has also been reported to essential social infrastructure, including airport facilities, hospitals and other public services, which remain intermittent or disrupted in some affected areas. Further clarity on figures and capacity are awaited from the NS. According to estimates from USGS, fatalities could surpass 10,000 people.

Following the launch of the DEC Venezuela Earthquake Appeal on 1 July 2026, the British Red Cross received confirmation of its first allocation of £1,614,684 (the highest of all DEC members). This funding will be received by BRC and sent to IFRC, who are managing this funding from through their country team and regional office. The Venezuela Red Cross has decided to allocate the minimum required of 30% to Phase 1, resulting in a budget of £484,405 from DEC. The remaining funding will be utilised during Phase 2 from January 2027 onwards and will be incorporated into a separate grant agreement once planning for that phase begins in November 2026. For DEC grants, a maximum member agency management fee of 7% is permitted, which is retained by IFRC. To meet Dear Ms Mei Lin Leon, IFRC's PSSR requirement of 7.5%, BRC will provide a top-up of the remaining 0.5% from appeal funds (£2,055.00), amounting to a total PSSR of £30,831. This brings the total to the amount specified in this grant agreement. This first payment is 1 of 3 planned payments for Phase 1 of £208,000 as per the agreed GAD. The second payment will be made later in the month.

In response to this emergency, the British Red Cross launched an Appeal to raise funds for our Disaster Fund. Following the launch of the DEC Appeal, our Appeal was upgraded to a restricted appeal. This grant is made up of two contributions: 1. £150,000 Disaster Fund allocation 2. £143,250 from Jersey Overseas Aid This grant is inclusive of IFRC PSSR contributions. Standard IFRC Appeal reporting will be required for these grants, which can be accessed via IFRC Go.
